classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the area using the perpendicular legs, then recognise the same area with BC as a different base and reverse the area formula to find AX; part a supplies the intermediate area.

content.prompt: Triangle $ABC$ has side lengths $AC=4\text{ cm}$, $AB=3\text{ cm}$ and $BC=5\text{ cm}$. $\angle BAC=90^\circ$. The point $X$ is on $BC$ and $AX$ is perpendicular to $BC$. Find:

answer.worked:
$AB$ and $AC$ are perpendicular.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }ABC&=\frac12\times AB\times AC\\\text{Area of }ABC&=\frac12\times3\times4\\\text{Area of }ABC&=6\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$\dfrac{12}{5}\text{ cm}=2.4\text{ cm}$

Use $BC$ as the base and $AX$ as its perpendicular height.
answer.worked:
Using base $BC=5\text{ cm}$, the perpendicular height is $AX$.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Area of }ABC&=\frac12\times BC\times AX\\6&=\frac12\times5\times AX\\AX&=\frac{2\times6}{5}\text{ cm}\\AX&=\frac{12}{5}\text{ cm}\\AX&=2.4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
